qualification_notes: A resident, not a trial: this configuration publishes the daytime service ID and the local-active compatibility alias, so every client that was told to send daytime reaches it, and it answers nighttime as well. One loaded model offers every service ID the router contract documents, so no client is left with nothing to send. Selecting it, and switching away from it, remain the operator's acts.

nighttime is answered by this same backend rather than by a second loaded model. A request that used the Everyday resident for the abliterated model's unfiltered behaviour is served here and redirected nowhere; the pictures it used to be the only resident that could read are read here as well, since the encoder joined this container on 2026-10-16. The filtered/unfiltered distinction the two 27B residents drew is carried by capability_profile.nsfw, which is false for this quant, and not by a second resident.

models.quantization: ISTA-DASLab GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS (3.25-bit i-quant, 70.6 GiB in two shards, 47.0 of them this configuration's own)
qualification_notes: Measured on 2026-10-20 on this machine (ops/reports/20261020-daisy-strata-feasibility/): IQ3_XXS warm 78-97 tok/s at 96.8-97.3 % expert-cache hits with 14.7 GiB of host RAM free, against IQ3_S at 7.6 GiB free and 87.8 % hits, which is the tier the engine itself calls tight and which parked on its own 8 GiB breaker. The window is capped at 65,536 rather than the trained 131,072 because the smaller quant fills each card with cached experts and aborts on a ~127k prompt at the full window: SIGABRT in prefill, exit -6, reproduced twice, ten minutes of arena reload after each. The alternative that keeps 128k alive was measured the same day, a 2,048 MiB per-card reserve, and it costs 13-18 % of warm decode and 26 % of the resident experts; this machine is a fast short-context box instead, on purpose, and its answer hashes came back byte-identical to the 3.5-bit tier's on both fixed-greedy cells, so nothing was given up in what the model says.

Nothing here is a number copied from the other machine. No --vram-reserve-mib, because the window cap is the fix that was chosen instead. No --resident-budget-gib, because the arm was measured with the engine's own sizing and a 55 GiB ceiling belongs to a box with 123 GiB of RAM. The conversation cache is stated off, and its floor is stated with it at 12,288 MiB because what the entry point writes sits in the workspace until a configuration says otherwise: with the pack pinning about 40 GiB of this machine's 60.7, a parked conversation may not spend any of the last 12 GiB of the 14.7 it leaves free. No control vector: the refusal direction is mounted and verified on the other host and was not part of any arm measured here.
